result.summary: Verified branch feature/WF02-REQ-001a, working tree clean (no remaining artifacts to stage). git fetch origin master confirmed origin/master (5cc6ba8) is a strict ancestor of HEAD; git rebase origin/master was a no-op ('Current branch feature/WF02-REQ-001a is up to date'), zero conflicts, zero commits rewritten. Plain git push origin feature/WF02-REQ-001a succeeded (fast-forward, d26beaa..351cdd8). Created PR #5 (gh authenticated as tvolodi) with the specified title/body, base master / head feature/WF02-REQ-001a. gh pr checks 5 --watch: build PASS on both required check runs (1m20s, 1m16s); deploy-prod/deploy-qa correctly 'skipping' (PR context, not a push to master). gh pr merge 5 --squash --delete-branch: the GitHub-side merge succeeded (confirmed via gh pr view 5 --json state,mergedAt -> MERGED at 2026-08-27T06:01:49Z, mergeCommit 69b7958851de1e3a8a488b9c9a6d74bd9a15b041; remote feature branch confirmed deleted) but gh's local side-effect (fast-forwarding this checkout to master) failed with 'Not possible to fast-forward' because local master held 11 unpushed WF-01 commits predating this branch (exactly as flagged in this handoff's own task.description) while origin/master had advanced by exactly the one new squash-merge commit -- a genuine two-sided divergence, not the documented worktree-variant scenario (git worktree list confirmed only one worktree) but the same root cause. Verified with git merge-tree/log that the two commit sets touch no overlapping content in a way that couldn't be reasoned about, then ran a real trial merge: git merge origin/master surfaced exactly 5 conflicted files (at, not over, the protocol's <=5 hand-resolve threshold): docs/agents/requirements.yaml, docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, handoffs/WF02-REQ-001a/step-00-git-setup.json, handoffs/orchestrator.log, handoffs/registry.json. Hand-read every conflict (this was git merge, not rebase, so --ours/--theirs kept normal merge meaning): all 5 resolved to 'take origin/master's side in full' because in every case origin/master's content was a strict superset or the objectively later-correct version of local master's stale/stub content (DOC-UPDATER's status:done + '.lang a' corrections in requirements.yaml; append-only done event in requirement_status.yaml; the real completed step-00 handoff vs a pending stub; and the fuller orchestrator.log/registry.json history) -- confirmed via direct diff against local master's version before resolving, not assumed. No local-only content was discarded: local master's 11 WF-01 commits are fully preserved as merge-parent history. Completed the merge (commit 7e7f570), then re-ran npm run lint (0 errors, 4 pre-existing warnings, matching RELEASE-VALIDATOR's earlier finding) and npm run build (exit 0, Turbopack, route table shows /[locale], /health, Proxy/Middleware registered) per the protocol's post-conflict-resolution verification step -- both green. Pushed the merge commit with a plain git push origin master (fast-forward, 69b7958..7e7f570, no force needed since this added a real merge rather than rewriting history). git fetch origin --prune removed the now-stale local remote-tracking ref for the deleted feature branch. Final state verified: git branch --show-current = master, git log --oneline -1 = 7e7f570 (merge commit whose second parent is the PR #5 squash-merge 69b7958), git status clean and up to date with origin/master, feature branch absent both locally and on origin.
